title: The classes of Stygia
summary: How the Hierarchy orders the society of the dead.

claims.text: The Hierarchy presents itself as strong, all-seeing and the only shield between the Restless and Oblivion.
It rules a society of ranks: the weakest wraiths become thralls or raw material for the forges, while most citizens work hard and hope superiors will promote them.

title: Death's history
summary: How the Underworld grows from the disasters of the living.

claims.text: Stygian history mirrors the living world's, but tracks the growth of death rather than of life; war, plague, famine and disaster feed the Underworld.
Like any mirror the match is imperfect, and the history of Stygia departs in many ways from the world seen through the Shroud.

title: Magisterium Veritatis and the Unlidded Eye

claims.text: Charon founded the Council of Inquisitors, the Magisterium Veritatis, with the Order of the Unlidded Eye as its knights, first to root Heretics out of Stygia; it now hunts Renegades and traitors as well.
Its knights wear the mask of the Grim Reapers for life; the mask is said to let them see into souls and to drive them to bring traitors to justice.

title: The Anacreon revolts
summary: Necropoli drifting from Stygia after Charon vanished.

claims.text: In 1931 an Anacreon of the Silent Legion in Boston resigned, protesting that Stygia ignored the Shadowlands beyond its borders while the mortal crisis stretched local Legions past their limits.
Some Necropoli became nearly independent, their Legions loyal to local Anacreons; others answered with harsher security, or with the look of autonomy without a true break.
After more than 20 years the Deathlords accepted that Charon would not return, and talk turned to which of them might be made Emperor, with the Smiling Lord favored.

title: Quarrels over souls
summary: How the Deathlords divide the dead.

claims.text: The Skeletal Lord's palace, the Seat of Dust, is a bone-white hall for victims of plague and famine, more solid than it looks.

Since Charon vanished, the division of souls among the Deathlords is disputed: the Lords of violence and pestilence never lack souls, while the Ashen Lady complains that longer human lives shrink the harvest owed to the Ashen Lady.
The Storm Maidens, called Valkyries or Amazons by outsiders, charge into Maelstroms to fight Spectres and take fewer losses than their recklessness ought to cost.
The Order of the Gray Knights, older and proven servants of the Ashen Lady, serve as honor guards and escorts for high-ranking wraiths.

title: The Hierarchy on werewolves
summary: What Stygia thinks of the Garou.

claims.text: Stygian officials know the Silent Striders travel the ways of the dead, and fear that Garou can bind spirits into objects and often see wraiths as foes.

Most werewolves count wraiths as creatures of the Wyrm, but some in the Hierarchy suspect the Wyrm the Garou describe is something like a Malfean, making them possible distant allies against Oblivion.
